extracted.intended_audience: manufacturers, private labelers, industry counsel, and other stakeholders affected by CPSC section 6(b) disclosures; CPSC staff
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed revisions to the CPSC's 6(b) regulation governing when the Commission must provide notice and opportunity to comment before publicly disclosing information about consumer products and related procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports of harm posted on SaferProducts.gov excluded from section 6(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supplemental NPR proposes including reports of harm posted on the publicly available consumer product safety information database (SaferProducts.gov) in the list of information not subject to section 6(b)(1) because section 6A(f)(1) of the CPSA specifically excludes such reports from the provisions of section 6(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exclusion applies only to reports that are published on SaferProducts.gov; reports of harm that are not published on SaferProducts.gov require the Commission to provide firms with any requisite 6(b) notice. The Commission may release or identify information contained in a posted SaferProducts.gov report without 6(b) notice only if (1) the Commission does not characterize the information contained in the report, and (2) the Commission's use of SaferProducts.gov information is accurate and not misleading. Example: stating 'SaferProducts.gov received 15 reports of harm involving Manufacturer ABC's lamp' is permissible; issuing a warning to consumers based on the report (e.g., 'stop using the lamps') would trigger the need for 6(b) notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicly available information exception (limited and qualified)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission proposes that section 6(b)(1) does not apply to 'Information that has already been made available to the public through sources other than the Commission, provided the Commission clearly indicates the source of the information and the Commission's use of the information is accurate and not misleading.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission may release or identify information obtained from public sources (e.g., news clippings) without 6(b) notice only if (1) the Commission does not characterize the publicly available information or relay new information, and (2) its use of the information is accurate and not misleading. Integrity of the source may be relevant (e.g., reputable newspaper). Example of impermissible use: a social media post that implies the Commission considers the article a basis for action (which would require 6(b) notice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Information substantially the same as previously disclosed (modified test)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements of section 6(b)(1) do not apply to 'Information, not previously disclosed, that in context does not disclose materially more or materially different information about the consumer product than what the Commission previously disclosed in accordance with the law.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under this approach the Commission need not provide a new 6(b) notice for disclosures that do not materially add to previously disclosed information. Example: a Commissioner may repeat findings that appeared in a published CPSC report (for which 6(b) notice was given). By contrast, discussing additional staff findings not in the published report would require separate 6(b) notice. The rule is contextual and focused on whether the new disclosure reveals materially more or different information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press releases issued by firms not separately enumerated as an exception
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supplemental NPR proposes to delete a specific provision that listed 'Press releases issued by firms' as a category of information not subject to section 6(b)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission's view is that it is unnecessary to single out firm press releases in the regulation because application of the general principles (e.g., publicly available information exception) governs whether firm press releases can be used without 6(b) notice. The deletion does not change the general legal analysis but removes the explicit standalone entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'public' and who is not 'public'
rubrics_metrics.description: For the requirements of section 6(b) to apply, the Commission (or any member, employee, agent, or representative in an official capacity) must propose to disclose information 'to the public.' The Supplemental NPR clarifies who is not considered part of the 'public' by listing 'Persons, including but not limited to, consumers, manufacturers, private labelers, retailers, or distributors.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contacting consumers, distributors, or retailers to discuss incidents or to investigate does not constitute disclosure 'to the public' when the information pertains to a particular consumer or particular distributor/retailer. The provision is intended to make clear that targeted communications about named parties are not public disclosures under §1101.12.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable person standard for whether the public can readily ascertain identity
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reasonable person who lacks specialized expertise can readily ascertain the identity of the firm from the information proposed to be disclosed, the Commission will provide such information to the firm for section 6(b) comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Supplemental NPR proposes deleting a vague sentence and retaining the reasonable person standard. It also inserts clarifications that information about categories of products (so long as identity cannot readily be ascertained) and information about manufacturers that does not designate or describe a specific product are not within the scope of section 6(b)(1). The Commission will ensure information that reflects on safety of a class of products or on a manufacturer is accurate and not misleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic transmission of 6(b) notices (preferred method)
rubrics_metrics.description: To increase efficiency and reduce burdens, the regulation would authorize electronic 6(b) notices, direct Commission staff to transmit notices electronically when possible, and encourage electronic communication back to the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A new paragraph requires electronic transmission to the extent practicable to avoid mail delays. If electronic transmission is not practicable or receipt cannot be confirmed, the Commission will take appropriate steps (including U.S. mail or other delivery service). Cross-references clarify procedures if electronic transmission cannot be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission inclusion of manufacturer's/private labeler's comments in disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 6(b)(1) provides that 'the Commission may, and upon the request of the manufacturer or private labeler shall, include with the disclosure any comments or other information or a summary thereof submitted by such manufacturer or private labeler.' The Supplemental NPR proposes to conform §1101.21(b)(4) to the statute and require that requests regarding inclusion or withholding be made in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the proposed revision the Commission is not required to disclose a firm's comments unless the firm specifically requests disclosure. Requests to withhold must be in writing to assist staff with processing and tracking. The regulation removes the prior provision that automatically honored requests to withhold and instead requires firms to provide a basis (see separate criterion) when seeking nondisclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests to withhold comments must state a basis and identify portions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a manufacturer or private labeler objects to disclosure of its comments or a portion thereof, it must notify the Commission at the time it submits its comments and provide the basis for its request; if objecting to only a portion, the firm must identify with specificity those portions requested to be withheld.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclusive or blanket assertions that comments be withheld are insufficient. The Supplemental NPR revised earlier language that required a rationale to support withholding; now the firm must provide a basis. The Commission will continue to protect trade secrets and confidential commercial information under FOIA and CPSA standards. Firms should consult 16 CFR 1015.18 for FOIA withholding procedures and required submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renotification / subsequent disclosures policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will notify manufacturers/private labelers that 'no further request for comment will be sought' if the Commission intends to disclose information, not previously disclosed, that in context does not disclose materially more or materially different information than what the Commission previously disclosed in accordance with the law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides certainty that the Commission need not send another 6(b) notice before restating previously disclosed content (example: restating a CPSC news release issued after a prior 6(b) notice). The rule focuses on whether the later disclosure conveys materially more or different information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of notice must describe manner of disclosure and related details
rubrics_metrics.description: Current §1101.21(b)(2) requires inclusion in a section 6(b)(1) notice of 'A general description of the manner in which the Commission will disclose the information, including any other relevant information the Commission intends to include with the disclosure.' The Supplemental NPR refines and reorganizes related text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Supplemental NPR deletes a sentence about press-release renotification (addressed elsewhere) and cross-references the revised provisions describing when no further notice is required. The notice should give enough information about form and content of the intended disclosure so firms understand the nature of the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for comments and extension requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may provide additional time for comment, particularly for manufacturers/private labelers receiving voluminous or complex material. The proposed heading revision reads: 'Time for comment and requests for extension of time.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission expects comments by the stated deadline and ordinarily will disregard late submissions. The Supplemental NPR proposes requiring extension requests to be in writing and submitted at least 48 hours before the deadline. If the Commission shortens the response time due to a public health and safety finding, extension requests from the firm will not be granted except on the Commission's initiative. The Commission will endeavor to respond promptly to extension requests but the statute does not require a prompt response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances when notice and opportunity to comment is not practicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 6(b)(1) requires notice and opportunity to comment 'to the extent practicable.' The Supplemental NPR proposes adding examples of circumstances when notice is not practicable, including: (1) when the Commission has been unable, after a diligent search, to obtain contact information for the manufacturer or private labeler; and (2) when an extraordinary circumstance necessitates immediate disclosure to protect public health and safety while the Commission simultaneously pursues notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission will conduct thorough searches in internal databases and other sources; inability to locate contact information after diligent search may justify disclosure without prior notice. Emergency situations (e.g., undisclosed hazard discovered on a holiday weekend) may require immediate public warning while staff continues attempts to notify the firm. Even in these cases the Commission will take reasonable steps to assure accuracy and fairness and that disclosure is reasonably related to effectuating the purposes of the Acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission must ensure information disclosed is accurate and not misleading
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart D revisions emphasize the Commission's obligation to take reasonable steps to assure public disclosure of information is accurate and that disclosure is fair in the circumstances and reasonably related to effectuating the purposes of the Acts it administers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relying on publicly available sources, the integrity of the source is relevant in determining whether the Commission's use is accurate and not misleading. The Commission will ensure disclosures reflecting on product safety or a manufacturer are accurate and fair. Examples and cross-references: how the Commission may report counts from SaferProducts.gov without characterization, but may not issue public warnings without providing 6(b) notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of trade secrets, privileged, or confidential commercial information in comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supplemental NPR clarifies that the proposed revisions do not affect the Commission's treatment of trade secret, privileged, or confidential commercial or financial information that may appear in a firm's comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission will maintain protections delineated in the CPSA, FOIA, corresponding regulations, and applicable case law. Firms seeking withholding of such information should follow the Commission's FOIA regulation at 16 CFR 1015.18, which specifies the information required with any request to withhold trade secret or privileged or confidential commercial information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarifying technical and conforming edits for statutory alignment and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout multiple sections (§1101.11–§1101.31 and subparts) the Supplemental NPR proposes technical, conforming, and minor grammatical edits to align the regulation with statutory language (e.g., replace 'firm' with 'manufacturer or private labeler'; correct cross-references; update citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These edits are procedural and stylistic but affect clarity and consistency across the regulation. Examples include revising headings, replacing 'CPSIA' with 'CPSA' where appropriate, updating citations to 16 CFR parts, and redesignating paragraph numbers to reflect deletions and insertions.
